item.title: RANKED: Best places to live in the Capital Region for 2026
item.description: School and neighborhood review website Niche recently released its 2026 Best Places to Live in America rankings. The rankings include more than 230 cities and 18,000 locations across the United States.

item.title: Rotterdam welcomes new police leadership
item.description: The city of Rotterdam is holding a formal swearing-in ceremony to welcome the new police chief and deputy chief to the police department.

item.title: Gas prices nearing $4 per gallon across Capital Region
item.description: Gas prices have risen another several cents in the past week, marking three straight weeks of pain at the pump, according to updated data by GasBuddy.

item.title: HVCC to highlight girls in STEM event with annual event
item.description: Hudson Valley Community College is staying true to its traditions of empowering young girls to pursue technology and science-based careers by hosting the 12th Annual Girls in STEM event on March 28.

item.title: Willie Nelson-headlined Outlaw Music Festival returning to SPAC
item.description: The annual Outlaw Music Festival will be returning to Saratoga Performing Arts Center to send the 2026 summer off into the sunset.

item.title: Albany police investigate stabbing in Washington Park
item.description: An investigation is underway into a stabbing that happened in Albany's Washington Park on Friday afternoon.

item.title: Cause determined for fire that injured 2 in Schenectady
item.description: The origin and cause of a fire on Foster Avenue Thursday has been determined. The Schenectady Fire Department's Fire Investigation Unit ruled the fire as accidental due to a highly volatile chemical solvent coming into contact with an ignition source.

item.title: Albany mayor says all potholes to be filled in 10 days
item.description: On Friday, Albany Mayor Dorcey Applyrs announced a plan to address every pothole in the city in 10 days. Applyrs made the announcement alongside the Department of General Services.

item.title: Albany man sentenced for shooting at a group of people
item.description: A man was sentenced on Friday for shooting at a group of people near Lark and Orange Streets in Albany in 2021. Ishmiel Hairston will serve seven years in state prison, followed by five years of post-release supervision.

item.title: Troy residents rally against Flock cameras
item.description: A controversial surveillance program in Troy sparked protests on Friday evening, with residents rallying outside City Hall over the city’s use of Flock cameras.

item.title: 5th annual Woofstock Music Festival returning to Scotia
item.description: The Animal Protective Foundation (APF) has announced the return of the annual Woofstock Music Festival. The pet-friendly fundraiser will take place on Sunday, June 7, at Lions Pavilion in Scotia.

item.title: 40th annual Waterford Canal Festival to set sail in May
item.description: The Waterford Canal Festival will return to the historic waterfront of the Village of Waterford on Saturday, May 16. The free event will be celebrating its 40th anniversary with a full day of family-friendly activities to mark the annual opening of the New York State Canal System.

item.title: Queensbury man sentenced in multimillion-dollar fraud scheme
item.description: A Queensbury man has been sentenced for a wire fraud conspiracy committed in connection with the operation and collapse of his alleged commercial lending business, Prime Capital Ventures, LLC. 46-year-old Kris Roglieri was sentenced to 97 months in prison.
